Fix the bond relay's boot stall, spread its audit across steps, trim boot and per-step reads, and make the capacity ramp linear with 35% volume weight (#767)

* Make the capacity ramp linear and pay 35% of each lane pool on qualified volume

CAPACITY_CURVE_EXPONENT 2.0 -> 1.0: a miner backing a fraction of a max-swap fill earns that
fraction of its crown slice instead of the fraction squared, so a max-swap raise no longer
squares every miner's shortfall.

QUALITY_VOLUME_BETA 0.25 -> 0.35: more of each lane pool follows qualified volume, less
follows crown time.

* Reconcile the bond relay once at boot and skip the settled read for a miner with no bond

The startup barrier's pass is a full reconcile, but the periodic clock started at zero, so
maybe_reconcile repeated the whole vault walk in the same forward step. On mainnet (114 bound
miners, three serial vault reads each, ~0.34s per read) that made the boot step ~300s, which the
forward stall watchdog kills, so a validator that restarted for any reason could not come back.

A miner with no bond nets to zero whatever its fee state, so compute no longer reads its settled
total: two vault reads instead of three for the ~80% of bound miners that never bonded.

* Read a miner's bond and lock in one batched message, paced under the subtensor rate limit

The relay's audit reads the vault for every bound miner. The bond and lock reads now travel as one
JSON-RPC batch answered at a single block (BondVaultClient.get_bond_state), which halves the round
trips per miner. The endpoint still meters each call in a batch — unpaced batches at ~11 calls/s
were rate-limited by Dwellir inside ten seconds — so flush holds successive miners 0.5s apart,
about 6 requests/s against a 10 requests/s plan. A lone event-driven read never waits.

A failed batch is unknown for both reads and is not retried call by call; a runtime too old for
batched runtime calls falls back to serial reads.

* style: auto-fix pre-commit hooks

* Walk the bond relay's audit a few miners per step after the boot pass

The full vault walk still runs once at boot, behind the startup barrier. After that the periodic
repair no longer re-reads every bound miner in one forward step: the bound set is a ring walked
once per reconcile interval, and each step marks dirty only the miners due by then, for that
step's own flush to re-read. Every miner is still re-checked once an interval, a lap that fell
behind is finished at its boundary, and a new lap rediscovers who is bound. The only new state is
the ring and a position in it.

* Harden the relay's batched read and audit ring after review

- A batch that fails for any reason is read again one call at a time. The lone read is the path
  the SDK retries and fails over, so an endpoint that refuses batches, drops the socket or
  rate-limits no longer leaves every miner unreadable and the startup barrier shut.
- A boot audit whose bindings read failed no longer comes back clean over an empty map.
- The boot audit seeds the ring's first lap instead of rediscovering the bound set in the same tick.
- A miner the ring has not seen is read as its lap opens, so a mid-lap binding waits at most one
  interval for its first audit, as before the ring.
- A wall clock stepped back can no longer produce a negative slice that marks most of the ring.
- The vault's u64 and lock decoders are shared by the lone and batched reads, and pacing takes an
  injectable timer so its test does not depend on real elapsed time.

* Start the stall watchdog with the loop, and trim boot and per-step chain reads

Watchdog: its clock started at construction, so everything boot does before the loop (56s on a
typical mainnet boot, 269s on a slow one) was charged to the first forward step. It now starts
when the loop does, and a finished forward pass counts as progress before the resync and weight
commit that follow it.

Boot: confirming the axon serve reads our own neuron (2 requests) instead of re-syncing the whole
metagraph (8), and the bond relay's subtensor connection is dialled on a thread while the chain
providers are checked.

Per step: every subnet alpha is priced by one get_subnet_prices read (4 requests) instead of one
read per declared alpha (2 requests each, about a hundred of them on a cold cache), falling back
to the per-leg read if it fails. The live crown snapshot reads lane-independent state once per
walk instead of once per quoted lane, and its Postgres deletes go out in one pipeline.

* Probe each EVM network once at boot and check independent backends side by side

A validator's startup check asked every provider's backend in turn: about 70 HTTP calls, one after
another, ~15s on mainnet. Two things made that longer than it had to be.

Several assets share an EVM network and each dialled it again: Ethereum five times, BNB and Polygon
twice, three calls a time. The network probe is now shared down a network's assets the way the
subtensor's already is for TAO and the alphas. connect_network only reads, so an asset that skips it
holds the state it would after running it; the signing key and each token's contract probes stay per
asset. The '[<Network>Rpc] connected' line is logged once per network instead of once per asset.

The backends are independent, so their checks now overlap: one lane per backend, serial within it,
at most four in flight. The subtensor's lane (TAO and every alpha) runs on the calling thread, so the
rate-limited keyed endpoint keeps a single caller. Constructors stay on the calling thread in
registry order, and results are admitted in registry order, so the providers dict and the failure
that stops a boot are what they were. Without check=True nothing is threaded.

One difference on a failing boot: the rows after the one that fails are now built and checked before
the error is raised, where the serial loop stopped at it.

* Refresh subnet alpha prices every 15 minutes instead of once per scoring window

One read now prices every alpha, so the crown checks that value a lane's alpha leg no longer need
to share the hourly scoring window: 16 requests an hour buys prices at most 15 minutes old.
